fact: The government's "Zéro donnée à l'extérieur" chantier, one of the twelve digital-transformation chantiers to 2030, aims to host platforms and data on national territory, and the Prime Minister's half-year evaluation of 25 July 2026 reported it as under implementation.

The ministry reported 120 public platforms inventoried for hosting in the country, the two inaugurated data centres being the destination, with repatriation begun and targeted for completion before end-2026; the document counts no body as having moved.
ANPTIC's board chair set as the course for 2026 the repatriation of administrations' and institutions' data to the national data centres inaugurated in January 2026; no body is stated to have moved.

The Prime Minister inaugurated two modular government-cloud data centres on 23 January 2026 as a key step of the strategic chantier "zéro donnée à l'extérieur", aimed at hosting, operating and securing all public data and repatriating data still stored abroad.
The Primature states the two government-cloud data centres inaugurated on 23 January 2026 are to host all public data under the "zéro donnée à l'extérieur" chantier; no body is stated to have moved.

The government presented a roadmap of 12 digital projects at a government seminar on 25 August 2025, the first-listed including repatriating and securing sensitive data under the principle "zero data abroad", guaranteeing national information is hosted locally.

The director general of digital transformation says a Prime Minister's circular enjoins the various actors to give priority to hosting at national level, and that requests for platform operation are screened for where data is hosted; the circular's own date is not given, so the interview's published date of 2026-03-03 is used.
